name: Tiramisu with Cooked Egg Yolks
desc: Moka pot espresso ladyfingers layered with mascarpone, whipped cream and gently cooked sweetened egg yolks.

source.title: Tiramisu
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1 cup (240 ml) strong espresso, brewed in a moka pot
2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, for dusting

steps: Brew the espresso, pour it into a shallow bowl, and cool to room temperature.

Set a heatproof bowl over a pot of barely simmering water without letting it touch the water. Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt constantly until pale, thick and foamy and 160°F on an instant-read thermometer, about 5 min. Take off the heat and cool 10 min.
Whip the cold cream and vanilla on medium-high to medium peaks, about 3 min.
In a large bowl, beat the mascarpone a few seconds to loosen it, then fold in the whipped cream until smooth.
Fold in the cooled yolk mixture until no streaks remain.
Dip half the ladyfingers in the espresso, a quick 1-second dunk per side, and lay them in a single layer in a 9x13 in dish, trimming to fill gaps.
Spread half the cream over them. Dip the remaining ladyfingers, layer them on top, and spread on the rest of the cream.
Dust heavily with cocoa through a fine-mesh sieve. Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hr, up to 1 day, until set.
tips: Dip fast so the ladyfingers do not go soggy.
The reel shows the method but no amounts. The amounts follow Sally's Baking Addiction's tiramisu with its egg whites left out, which cooks the yolks the same way.
Cooking the yolks to 160°F makes them safe to eat. Sally's cooks them until light and foamy without naming a temperature.
